newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom assets frozen for $2.8 bln back tax.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom assets frozen for $2.8 bln back tax.

text.p: The Russian government has frozen sizable assets of gas monopoly RAO Gazprom in an attempt to recover more than 15 trillion roubles ($2.8 billion) in unpaid taxes, Gazprom's chairman said.

"The accounts of Yugtransgaz have been frozen and assets inventoried (for possible auction). The same thing is happening at Uraltransgaz, Urengoigazprom and a number of other firms," Rem Vyakhirev said in a letter to the Federation Council upper house of parliament released on Wednesday.
Urengoigazprom, a Gazprom unit, is one of Russia's largest producers of natural gas.
The timing of the move is particularly unwelcome as Gazprom, Russia's biggest corporation, is due to announce the terms of an international share placement in the next few days.

Gazprom, where Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov both worked before joining the government, has been viewed as a state within a state and tax payments are low in relation to income.
The government has promised to clamp down on all tax evasion to meet the terms of a $10 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund.

Vyakhirev said Russia was treating Gazprom like a kulak, referring to Soviet government campaigns in the 1920s and 1930s in which well-to-do private farmers, or kulaks, were stripped of their grain and later driven off their land.
Gazprom said the government was forcing it to sell gas at low prices and to carry three times as much in debts, some of which are owed by the government, as it owed, while being squeezed for taxes.
Vyakhirev called on the Ministry of Finance and Central Bank to net out debts between companies and called for cuts in the price of oil, metals and rail tariffs in line with natural gas.
He also raised the possibility that Gazprom would call for accounts of its own debtors to be frozen.
"Following the logic of freezing accounts, why not do the same with the Gazprom's debtors?" the letter said.
The amount of money owed to Gazprom rose to 48.7 trillion roubles at the start of July this year from 13.9 trillion roubles a year earlier.
